Term1: Prophylaxis against mycobacterium avium disease in persons with hiv/aids
Text:
# PROPHYLAXIS AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM DISEASE IN PERSONS WITH HIV/AIDS

Infectious Diseases should be involved in all cases. Patients with CD4 count < 50 cells per microliter, after ruling out disseminated MC disease, should receive prophylaxis until CD4 count is >100 for at least 3 months in response to antiretroviral therapy.

References:

- Guidelines for Prevention and Treatment of Opportunistic Infections in HIV
- Infected Adults and Adolescents. AIDSinfo (2015) 1-282
- Mandell chapter: Mycobacterium avium complex
- Sanford keyword: Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare
- Up-to-Date article: Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infections in HIV-infected patients
Therapy:
## Preferred prophylaxis

Azithromycin 1200 mg PO q week ($) [M]

## Alternative

Clarithromycin 500 mg PO BID ($) [R,DI]
Outpt: ORZID3 GMENU PATH PRO M. AVIUM W/ HIV
